key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Gradual over months to years. LOCATION: Upper airway. DURATION: Chronic, persistent. CHARACTER: Episodic breathing cessation during sleep. AGGRAVATING: Supine position, alcohol, sedatives. RELIEVING: CPAP, weight loss, positioning. TIMING: Nocturnal, episodic. SEVERITY: Mild to moderate (3-6/10). ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Loud snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime sleepiness, fatigue, morning headaches. KEY POSITIVES: Loud snoring, witnessed apneas, daytime sleepiness. KEY NEGATIVES: No chest pain, no wheezing.
